revised_comments: Madagascar's ministries of Agriculture, Livestock and Digital Development launched a national digital public infrastructure for agriculture in June 2026, supported by the World Bank via the KWPF mechanism. The infrastructure is explicitly designed to ensure interoperability and data sovereignty across agricultural, livestock and fisheries data. Three initial digital services are under development: a national farmer registry, a combined price-monitoring and weather-alert service, and a digital agricultural advisory platform, being built by three selected firms under a technical adviser. Related digital livestock initiatives (beehive and cattle health monitoring) are also under way. Technical integration with the national data exchange platform has not yet been publicly confirmed.

revision_notes: Original score of 0 relied on a Russian-language e-governance handbook listings page that does not itself discuss Madagascar's justice-sector integration. Fresh reporting on the official national launch of the Rahaka interoperability platform (28 April 2026) confirms the system is already operational with the Ministry of Justice, alongside EDBM, CNaPS, INSTAT and the tax directorate (DGI), under the first Rahaka usage convention signed by the Digital Governance Unit (UGD), several ministries and private actors, backed by decree n°2025-1959. Score raised from 0 (Unknown) to 4 (Partially integrated) given confirmed operational status for the Ministry of Justice among the first cohort of connected agencies at this early phase.
revised_comments: Madagascar's national data exchange platform, Rahaka (built on X-Road), was officially launched on 28 April 2026 under decree n°2025-1959 governing interoperability of public information systems. As of launch, the Ministry of Justice is one of five confirmed operational participants, alongside the Economic Development Board (EDBM), the social security fund (CNaPS), the national statistics institute (INSTAT) and the tax directorate (DGI). This represents partial integration of justice-sector data into the national exchange, achieved through the first Rahaka usage convention signed between the Digital Governance Unit, several ministries and private-sector actors.

A public interoperability framework document sets out governance principles including transparency. However, there is no public dashboard or dedicated periodic report on the exchange's operations, participating agencies' data flows or performance, limiting disclosure to launch announcements and legal texts rather than ongoing public reporting.
